newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai court acquits former PM Anand Panyarachun.
newsitem.headline: Thai court acquits former PM Anand Panyarachun.

text.p: A Thai court on Friday acquitted former prime minister Anand Panyarachun on a malfeasance charge but sentenced three co-defendants to suspended two-year jail terms, an official said.

Prawit Khamparat, a former Supreme Court chief judge in 1992, filed a suit against then-premier Anand, and the justice minister, president of the Supreme Court and permanent secretary of the justice ministry at the time.
"The court has ordered the acquittal of prime minister Anand but sentenced his co-defendants to two years' suspended jail terms," a court official said.

Prawit accused the four of neglecting their duty by failing to comply with a 1992 decree on the annual reshuffle of judges. As a result, he said, he was deprived of a promotion to head the Region One Appeals Court.
Friday's decision came after more than four years of hearings.

Anand is a respected diplomat who served as interim prime minister in 1991 until new elections could be held after a bloodless military coup overthrew the Chatichai Choonhavan government in February 1991.
He was appointed caretaker prime minister in May 1992 after an outbreak of political violence, and he served in the post for several months until new elections were held.
Anand did not comment after the verdict.
